% Pattern: head/command/article. A command of the paper with no argument that
% starts a paragraph and writes a head in a font, as \claim, writes an
% unnumbered item at each call. A head number written with a reference takes
% the number of the label, and a proof head can follow \end{lemma} on its
% line.
% from math/0406514
% want lem-1 statement/lemma 1.1 labels=one
% want head-1 statement/theorem 1.1A
% want head-2 statement/claim -
% want lem-2 statement/lemma 1.2
% want head-3 proof -
% want head-4 statement/theorem 1B'
\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{lem}{Lemma}[section]
\newcommand{\claim}{{\noindent \bf Claim }}
\newcommand{\Thm}{\textbf{Theorem}}
\begin{document}
\section{One}
\begin{lem}\label{one} Each finite tree has a leaf. \end{lem}

\smallskip \noindent {\bf Theorem {\ref{one}A}} {\em Each finite graph has a vertex.}

\claim The set of leaves is not empty.
\begin{lem} Each path is a tree. \end{lem} \proof Clear.

\noindent {\bf Theorem 1B'} {\em Each cycle has an edge.}

\Thm{} is a word in this sentence.
\end{document}
